summary: The change is a one-literal default flip plus a cleanup effect inside the existing orchestrator, not a new feature. In UI/SidekickMenu/SidekickMenu.tsx change the destructured default from `searchEnabled = true` to `searchEnabled = false`; the existing render guard `searchEnabled && !effectiveRailCollapsed` then stops mounting the input, its ref stays null, and the existing autofocus effect already no-ops on a null ref, so no new focus code is needed. Add one small useEffect that dispatches `SET_SEARCH_TERM` with an empty string whenever `searchEnabled` is false and a term is still held, which unfilters the list (getFilteredItems returns the input unchanged for an empty term) and lets the existing pre-search path effect restore the section; SET_SEARCH_TERM is already in the reducer, so no reducer or context change is needed. Enabled search keeps the same lookup, placeholder, icon, autofocus, empty-state, arrow-key and numbered-shortcut code paths untouched, because only the default value and the off-state guard change. Public surface is unchanged (no export, prop name or type is added, removed or renamed; SidekickMenuProps.searchEnabled remains `boolean | undefined`), so this is a behaviour-breaking change: package.json goes to 2.0.0 and docs/breaking-changes.md gets a v2.0.0 entry with the searchEnabled={true} migration snippet, while README.md, docs/api.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/examples.md and docs/features.md stop presenting search as on by default. Scale: nothing new scales with menu size; with search off the component mounts no input and performs no non-empty filtering, and with search on the existing memoized per-level filtering is unchanged, so a hundred times more items behaves exactly as 1.7.0. Cost: one boolean comparison and one effect check per render, no new state, listeners, timers, storage keys, network calls, dependencies, CSS or files; the default flip can only shrink or leave equal the bundle, so the dist/index.js and dist/index.esm.js sizes are measured before and after against 1.7.0 and no .size-limit.json exists to raise. Tests: characterization coverage comes first by running the existing suite unchanged, then the four existing search tests in UI/SidekickMenu/SidekickMenu.test.tsx opt in with searchEnabled={true}, and new tests assert the input is absent with default props (placeholder query and an input-element query), present with searchEnabled, that the autofocus effect does not throw or move focus when search is off, and that setting searchEnabled from true to false while a term is typed drops the term and restores the unfiltered list.
